dedupe_keys.name: satellite drag and operations during the may 2024 gannon storm parker and linares 2024

description: This case study examines how the May 2024 Gannon geomagnetic storm, the largest in more than 20 years, affected satellite operations in low Earth orbit, where the population has surged since the last major storm in 2003 with commercial services and proliferated constellations. William Parker and Richard Linares of MIT wrote it as a short note on arXiv in June 2024 (revised July 2024). They assess the forecast performance of the ap geomagnetic index, finding that the magnitude and duration of the storm were poorly predicted even one day ahead, and they identify thermospheric mass density enhancements by tracking the drag decay of objects in the full NORAD two-line element history for LEO. Coverage is the whole tracked LEO population. Format and access: a preprint on arXiv. Licence: arXiv distribution licence; free to read. Caveats: TLE-derived decay is coarse, and the note is an early analysis written weeks after the event. It supports resilience planning for space traffic management and satellite collision risk during storms. Related catalogue records are the CelesTrak orbital element sets it builds on and the 2024 solar maximum operator mitigation study.
